title: Kitty tells the truth: restore, automations, and the deadline alert
description: Three verified defects where Kitty reports success it did not achieve or quietly loses what Jacob gave it. Restore claims to replace a backup and appends it instead, so restoring twice triples the data. The morning brief records completion even when no phone channel accepted it, and Jacob's edited brief time is overwritten from a config file on every restart. The deadline escalation that the phone-channel work exists for is fully implemented and never called by anything in production. Every premise was re-verified against origin/main 295b92fc33a3f1b93da86f3c6bb5fbb54e367105 before authoring. Selected by the 2026-08-31 product-director pass from finding IDs XCUT-B004, XCUT-B005, AUTO-B001, AUTO-B002, AUTO-B004, MOBILE-B001 and MAIL-B001.

packets.title: Restoring a backup gives back exactly what was backed up
packets.objective: gateway/storage_sync.py:187 import_all documents that it replaces every migrated store, but gateway/storage_sync.py:97 import_memories calls add_memory per record and the journal import behaves the same way, so restoring a snapshot appends to whatever is already there. Restoring the same file twice leaves three copies of every memory. Change import_all so each migrated store ends holding exactly the snapshot's records and nothing else, and make the operation safe to repeat. Separately, gateway/storage_sync.py:65 export_preferences is a placeholder returning an empty dict while the module advertises exporting user data, so every export silently omits preferences: return the real preference records. Do not change the snapshot file format version, and do not add a UI surface for backup or restore, which is an open product decision. This packet creates no new production files; every change lands in the modules named above.
acceptance_criteria: Importing the same snapshot twice leaves every migrated store with the same record count as importing it once.
After an import, each migrated store contains the snapshot's records and no record that was present only before the import.
export_preferences returns the stored preference records, and a preference present before an export round-trip is present after it.
A snapshot with a wrong or missing format version is still rejected exactly as it is today.
A failure part-way through an import reports what failed in plain language and does not leave a store holding a mixture of old and new records.
No new HTTP route, CLI command, or UI surface is introduced.
python -m pytest -q tests/test_storage_sync.py passes.

packets.title: Automations stop reporting success they did not achieve
packets.objective: Three linked untruths in scheduled work. First, gateway/brief_scheduler.py:125-133 logs a warning and returns the brief text even when push_to_jacob accepted on no channel, so gateway/automation_actions.py records the run as completed; the existing ACTION_RESULT_STATUSES vocabulary already has source_unavailable for this, so report that instead of completed when no channel accepted the brief. Second, gateway/app.py:292-298 calls cron.ensure_schedule on every gateway start using load_brief_time() from config/user_profile.json, and no route or UI writes that file, so an edited brief time is silently reverted on the next restart: startup must not overwrite a schedule a person has since changed. Third, gateway/cron.py:151-166 keys its duplicate check on the exact tuple of action, schedule_type, schedule_value and metadata, so editing one of the five seeded schedules changes the key and the next startup seeds a second copy; seeding must recognise an existing seeded schedule that has been edited rather than adding a duplicate. Keep every existing schedule and run row; do not delete or prune rows to resolve duplicates. This packet creates no new production files; every change lands in the modules named above.
acceptance_criteria: When no push channel accepts the morning brief, the automation run records source_unavailable rather than completed, and the reason is readable without knowing what a channel is.
When a push channel does accept the brief, the run still records completed exactly as it does today.
A brief time changed after first start survives a gateway restart unchanged.
A first start on a machine with no schedules still seeds the brief schedule from the profile.
Editing a seeded schedule and restarting the gateway leaves exactly one schedule for that action, not two.
No existing schedule row or automation run row is deleted by this change.
python -m pytest -q tests/test_brief_scheduler.py tests/test_cron.py tests/test_automation_actions.py tests/test_app_automation_supervision.py passes.
validation_commands: python -m pytest -q tests/test_brief_scheduler.py tests/test_cron.py tests/test_automation_actions.py tests/test_app_automation_supervision.py

packets.title: The deadline warning actually reaches the phone
packets.objective: gateway/deadline_watch.py exports check_and_push, which escalates an approaching deadline to Jacob's phone. Nothing in production calls it: gateway/app.py registers cron actions for brief.deliver, brief.refresh, insights.return_due, monitors.check, inbox.scan, traces.compact, mail.poll, github.poll, experts.poll and prefetch.warm, and the string deadline does not appear in that file at all. The two reachable manual paths are also wired off: gateway/routes/deadlines.py:49 post_sweep defaults push to False and its only caller in the UI sends no push argument, and the kitty launcher's sweep command at line 685 calls sweep(push_fn=None). Register the deadline watch as a scheduled automation action alongside the existing ones, and pass push through from both the sweep route and the CLI so pressing sweep or running the command does the whole job. Reuse the existing push facade and its quiet-hours and dedupe behaviour; do not add a second notification path, and do not change what counts as an approaching deadline. This packet creates no new production files; every change lands in the modules named above.
acceptance_criteria: A registered scheduled action runs the deadline watch and calls the push facade for a deadline inside the escalation window.
The sweep route escalates by default, and its response says how many deadlines were escalated.
The kitty sweep command escalates by the same path as the route, not a separate one.
With no push channel configured, the sweep reports plainly that nothing could be delivered and does not claim it escalated anything.
Quiet hours and duplicate suppression continue to behave exactly as the push facade already defines them; no second notification path is introduced.
A deadline outside the escalation window still produces no push.
python -m pytest -q tests/test_deadline_watch.py tests/test_brief_deadlines.py tests/test_cron.py passes.
